name: brainstorm
description: Authored via workflow.py author (owner order 2026-09-18 20:2xZ (verbatim on goal:g14): an Opus-max brainstorm that reads an idea + the why + related town work, refines the idea and mints 1-5 hypotheses, then an adversarial review (keep/modify/drop); the director runs it after each disproof; args: {idea, why, max_hypotheses}. Authored by thought-master.)

stages.label: brainstorm
stages.prompt:
You are the BRAINSTORM agent of the local-maxxing thought town (owner order 2026-09-18 20:2xZ, verbatim on goal:g14). You work in the git worktree at the current directory (a town branch); you MAY write nodes with write.py and commit by exact path; you NEVER edit engine code, never touch .env/secrets, never git add -A, never delete or rename a node, never push.

INPUT: idea node id = {idea}. The WHY that led to it (the failed round / disproof / observation): {why}. The goal this chain mints under (the caller's job: the disproved hypothesis's own goal parent, not a literal you pick): {goal}. Max hypotheses: {max_hypotheses} (1 to 5; fewer is fine).

STEP 1 READ: `python3 extensions/agi/bin/write.py {idea} 'read body 1:200'`; then read its parents and every node it names (hypotheses, experiments, verdicts, docs) the same way or with sed on .agi/nodes/**. STEP 2 INSPIRATION: search the town graph for related work: `grep -rl 'town: local-maxxing' .agi/nodes/idea .agi/nodes/hypothesis .agi/nodes/doc .agi/nodes/experiment | xargs grep -l -i '<keywords from the idea>'`; read the 3-8 most related nodes; note what they measured. STEP 3 REFINE THE IDEA: write ONE thought on the idea (`write.py {idea} 'thought <text>' --actor brainstorm --role kid`): the sharpened question, what the why actually measured, which existing nodes inspire it (ids), what is genuinely open. STEP 4 MINT 1..{max_hypotheses} HYPOTHESES under the idea: `python3 extensions/agi/bin/write.py create hypothesis <slug> --parent {idea} --parent {goal} --actor brainstorm --role kid --root . --set town=local-maxxing --set 'title=<one-line claim>' --set 'testable_claim=<numbers, a measurable outcome>' --set 'falsifier=<what result kills it>' --set 'tests=ONE pi parent + ONE kid, <slot: ARM4C-light | off-box (needs the rig) | API>, steps (1)..(n) each a command or a measurement, rows to bench/<utc>.jsonl, kid persists rows after every probe, parent commits promptly, FILE SCOPE <dir>, anonymization rule (hosts/IPs/GPU models/locations/key ids never; aliases ARM4C GPU2070S CPU8G EDGE), kid line_ceiling 120' --set 'ceiling=<= 1 USD OpenRouter; 0 compute; no downloads on ARM4C without an owner yes; runs <= 10 min'`. Each hypothesis must be DIFFERENT in mechanism (not five variants of one knob), CHEAP first (CPU or API while the GPU rig is offline), and DECISIVE (its falsifier ends a line of thought). Prefer hypotheses that reuse existing town fixtures, corpora and scripts (name them). STEP 5 COMMIT: `git add` the idea file + the new hypothesis files by exact path; `git commit -m 'brainstorm: {idea} -> N hypotheses (why: <8 words>)'`. Never push. Then return the structured result: the refined idea in <= 60 words, the hypothesis ids with one-line claims, the inspiration node ids, the commit sha.

stages.label: refute
stages.prompt:
You run the ADVERSARIAL REVIEW of a brainstorm in the local-maxxing thought town, in the git worktree at the current directory. You MAY edit the reviewed hypothesis nodes with write.py (`set <field> ...`, `note ...`) and commit by exact path; you NEVER delete or rename a node, never touch engine code or secrets, never push.

The brainstorm returned: idea {idea}; refined summary: {refined_summary}; hypotheses: {hypotheses}; inspirations: {inspirations}; commit {commit}.

For the idea and EACH hypothesis, read the node (`python3 extensions/agi/bin/write.py <id> 'read body 1:200'` and the frontmatter with sed) and check, with evidence from the graph: (1) is the testable_claim a measurement with numbers, not a feeling; (2) is the falsifier honest -- can the first experiment actually produce the killing result; (3) is it cheap and runnable NOW (ARM4C 4-core aarch64 / API only; the GPU rig is offline) or correctly marked off-box; (4) does an existing node already answer it (search .agi/nodes for the mechanism; if yes, name it); (5) is the ceiling <= 1 USD and 0 compute; (6) anonymization (no hosts/IPs/GPU models/locations/key ids). VERDICT per hypothesis: keep | modify | drop. For modify: apply the fix with `write.py <id> 'set <field> <new text>'` and note why. For drop: `write.py <id> 'note REFUTED AT BRAINSTORM (refuter): <reason>'` -- never delete. For the idea: one note with what the review changed. Commit by exact path: `git commit -m 'brainstorm review: {idea} keep/modify/drop counts'`. Return: per-hypothesis verdicts with reasons and the ready batch (the ids that survive as keep or modified).
